claims.text: Replica-exchange molecular dynamics coupled with metadynamics or umbrella sampling can accurately reconstruct the free-energy landscape of high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed combined sampling method can reconstruct this landscape efficiently across a wide range of HEA compositions.

A single reconstructed free-energy landscape can be used to determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties simultaneously.
The target materials are HEAs in solid-solution states near melting over multiple compositions.
The simulations will span the solid-to-liquid transition for diverse HEA compositions.
The reconstructed free-energy profile will contain barriers and minima corresponding to solid and liquid states.
Enhanced sampling will efficiently overcome kinetic barriers associated with the melting transition.
Thermodynamic parameters can be extracted from free-energy differences and integration along a melting reaction coordinate.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change will agree with high-resolution experiments to within 10%.
The method will provide detailed liquid-phase thermodynamic data.
The simulated free-energy barriers will provide an internal consistency check.
Conventional DSC has limited resolution across HEA compositional space.
Standard ab initio molecular dynamics is computationally prohibitive for the proposed family-wide thermodynamic characterization.
The method should perform well for HEAs having well-defined solid-liquid transitions and reliable interatomic potentials.
Extremely sluggish dynamics may degrade the performance of the proposed method.
Ambiguous phase boundaries or highly rugged free-energy landscapes may degrade the performance of the proposed method.
Experimental HEA literature reports melting temperature, heat of fusion, and liquid density values that can serve as thermodynamic reference data.

The approach is falsified if its thermodynamic predictions deviate from independent experimental measurements by more than approximately 10%, beyond combined uncertainties, across a representative HEA set.
